gen-press-start-2p-gf-parkinsans: Chunky pixel charm up top, with only a faint thick-and-thin shift you notice on a close look. Parkinsans keeps one stroke thickness throughout, with lowercase rising near the capitals, and the two sit together like an arcade sign beside a tidy label.
gen-press-start-2p-gf-pathway-extreme: Press Start 2P spaces its letters like cut-outs pinned far apart, with big open lowercase bowls. Pathway Extreme follows with stubby ascenders and descenders around a big x-height, so a longer passage moves along smoothly and stays easy on the eye.
gen-press-start-2p-gf-preahvihear: Press Start 2P sets its pinned-apart, cut-out style letters in the heading, with thin strokes about half the weight of the thick ones. Preahvihear keeps its lofty x-height open and easy going.
gen-press-start-2p-gf-prompt: Playful, with big open lowercase bowls and a faint thick-thin shift that shows on a close look, while Prompt gives an oversized, readable plain sans below. Retro spirit meets approachable clarity.
gen-press-start-2p-gf-pt-sans-caption: Press Start 2P brings widely spaced, cut-out letters with a subtle pen-like modulation in its bowls. And PT Sans Caption answers with big-bodied lowercase and unclosed, inviting curves, so the sans text feels roomier than the heading looks.
gen-press-start-2p-gf-puritan: Pixel-flavored fun in the heading, with letters pinned far apart and a low-to-medium contrast axis, sits above Puritan, whose rounded forms stay clearly open to the side. Both feel friendly, one retro and one plain sans.
gen-press-start-2p-gf-questrial: Questrial lays down open c, e and s shapes in strokes of a single weight, with a tall band of letters under short stalks. Press Start 2P brings the contrast, since its curves carry the slight thickening of a reed pen while Questrial stays flat and stencil-cut.
gen-press-start-2p-gf-radio-canada: Widely spaced letters, like cut-outs pinned apart, give the heading its look. Press Start 2P handles the playful retro flourish with medium contrast and no sharp hairlines, while Radio Canada, a plain sans, keeps tall, full c, s and z shapes in a line with no pressure variation.
gen-press-start-2p-gf-radio-canada-big: Chunky retro letters sit pinned far apart, with a light contrast between verticals and curves. And Radio Canada Big follows like glass tubing bent into letters, a monoline sans-serif whose terminals finish well clear of the stem.
gen-press-start-2p-gf-readex-pro: Press Start 2P pins its cut-out letters far apart. Readex Pro, a plain sans of tubular strokes like bent copper pipe, keeps a steady weight and broad terminal gaps, so a longer passage moves smoothly from word to word.
